classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the winning outcome across both players' turns, enumerate the stopping sequences of different lengths, sum their unequal probabilities, and reframe the five-turn event as the complement of uninterrupted play.

inlines.text: Bob and Mary compete against each other in a game that involves taking turns spinning a counter that has three possible outcomes

spec.sourceRegion: Centred spinner in Problem 7 on printed page 277.
spec.description: Unequal labelled sectors with an arrow from the central pivot into the upper-left of sector C. The source uses grey ordinary marks. The reconstruction uses house black.
spec.mathematics: A vertical diameter separates the left semicircle C from the right semicircle. A radius 18 degrees above the rightward horizontal separates upper-right A from lower-right B, giving sector proportions 0.2, 0.3 and 0.5.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete source figure is visible in the question.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How many ways can Bob win within three turns of the game overall? Write down the sequences of $A$, $B$ and $C$ representing these scenarios.

answer.worked: Bob wins as soon as a spin lands on $A$, whoever spins it. Every earlier spin must land on $C$ for the game to continue. The three sequences are $A$, $CA$ and $CCA$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence, find the probability of Bob winning within three turns of the game.

answer.worked:
Multiply the probabilities along each sequence of independent spins, then add because the three sequences are mutually exclusive.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{Bob wins within three turns})&=0.2+0.5\times0.2+0.5^2\times0.2\\P(\text{Bob wins within three turns})&=0.2+0.1+0.05\\P(\text{Bob wins within three turns})&=\frac{7}{20}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: What is the probability that somebody has won within the first 5 turns of the game overall?

answer.worked:
There is no winner after five turns only if all five independent spins land on $C$.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{no winner after five turns})&=0.5^5\\P(\text{no winner after five turns})&=\frac{1}{32}\\P(\text{a winner within five turns})&=1-\frac{1}{32}\\P(\text{a winner within five turns})&=\frac{31}{32}\end{align*}$$
